verdicts.why: The brief and persona answers confirm weekly spoilage of produce and two stockouts of noodles last month, directly indicating financial loss from over-ordering perishables and running out of staples.
The persona explicitly states 'ordering is guesswork' and the rough idea says 'ordering decisions come from numbers instead of gut feel,' grounding this statement directly.
The persona confirms invoices are entered when deliveries arrive and that the system should be fed by supplier invoices, making them a primary data input.
The persona explicitly describes a nightly stock count as part of the workflow and as a data feed for the system.
The rough idea explicitly calls for 'an inventory and budget tracker' as a combined single tool, grounding this decision.
The success criteria (spoilage waste halves, zero stockouts) directly imply that data-driven ordering will reduce waste and stockout costs, making this hypothesis grounded in stated goals.
The persona explicitly states that 'whichever cook closes does the nightly count on a phone,' so this is already a known fact, not an unknown.
The persona already answered this: invoices arrive as paper or PDF, so this is not an unknown but a known fact.
The persona explicitly stated about 60 ingredients, so the number of SKUs is already known, not an open question.
The persona answers do not mention a target budget period (daily, weekly, or monthly), so this remains a genuine unknown not addressed in the brief.

payload.why: The consultant asked zero questions, so the exported spec is almost entirely populated with vague paraphrases of the rough idea rather than the richer facts the persona was ready to supply. Critical specifics—60 ingredients, 15-item nightly count scope, two suppliers, per-invoice price history, Windows laptop + Android phone constraint, the 8 staple stockout metric, spoilage-halving success criterion, and the two-year history desire—are all absent, leaving the artifact insufficient to drive even a first vertical slice without major re-discovery work.
